articles.title: Oscilar CEO Neha Narkhede at Money2020 USA Importance of TransUnion Pact
articles.summary: At Money20/20 USA, Oscilar Co-Founder and CEO Neha Narkhede joins NYSE Live to discuss the growing challenges financial institutions face as artificial intelligence transforms both fraud prevention and fraud detection. Narkhede explains why Oscilar partnered with NYSE-listed TransUnion to address issues such as synthetic identity fraud and credit washing, and how combining fraud and credit risk signals can help institutions make more informed decisions. She discusses the challenges banks face when defending against increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled fraud tactics and why fragmented risk systems can make it harder to identify coordinated attacks. The conversation also explores agentic transactions, including how banks can verify AI agents, manage risk, and determine when human oversight remains necessary. Narkhede shares her perspective on balancing innovation with regulatory requirements and why explainable AI and real-time risk infrastructure are becoming increasingly important across financial services. articles.summary: This episode of NYSE Live features conversations on Federal Reserve policy, business leadership, financial technology, market structure, space innovation, and the evolving consumer landscape. Chief Economist Jeffrey Roach discusses what recent Federal Reserve commentary may signal ahead of the December meeting and the economic themes market participants are closely monitoring. Inc. Editor in Chief Mike Hofman joins the program to discuss the 2026 Best in Business Awards and the qualities that distinguish leading organizations. At Money20/20 USA, Oscilar CEO Neha Narkhede discusses the importance of the company's agreement with TransUnion and its role in advancing risk and decisioning capabilities. The episode also features Wall Street veteran Jay Woods explaining the mechanics behind Kraft Heinz's transfer to the New York Stock Exchange, while NYSE's Chris Bergan discusses why an increasing number of large-cap companies are choosing to transfer their listings to the NYSE. From the aerospace sector, a Redwire Space executive highlights the significance of the company's $40 million NASA moon base-related contract and its implications for future capabilities. Rounding out the program, WPP Media's Adam Arnegger joins Beet Retreat LA to discuss the evolution of the consumer journey and the factors influencing how brands connect with audiences in a rapidly changing media environment.
